media:group.media:title: Pretty Circles | She Stepped Off the Carousel (Official Animated Music Video) | R4agRek0il
media:group.media:description:
He's back on Monday with coffee and that half-smile. She forgives him. Again. 🎠 But the same blue tent keeps passing, and this time she is counting.
"Pretty Circles" is a dark fairground waltz-pop story about a love that goes fast but never goes far, and the quiet second she puts one foot on solid ground. Nobody is the villain here. Watch to the end. 👀
🔔 Subscribe to R4agRek0il for the next music video. 👍 Like if the chorus got stuck in your head, and tell me in the comments: what is YOUR "pretty circle"?
⏱ CHAPTERS 0:00 The hook 0:06 Intro: the music box 0:23 Verse 1: Sunday night, Monday morning 0:58 Pre-Chorus: "it feels so much like flying" 1:18 Chorus: "we go round in pretty circles" 1:40 Verse 2: "to where?" 2:15 Pre-Chorus 2 2:35 Chorus 2 2:57 Bridge: she lets go of the painted mane 3:14 Final Chorus: "I'm standing still, right here" 3:38 Outro: "you look so happy, going by"
🔵 THE BLUE TENT (spoilers) Everything on the ride is warm, bright and moving, so it feels like going somewhere. The blue tent is the one fixed thing outside it, and it comes back on the same line, lap after lap. It is the pattern made visible: the same fight, the same apology, the same Monday. It never changes, so it is the only honest witness in the song. "I know it far too well" is the moment she admits she has been counting laps. Blue is the colour of the cold, clear world beyond the ride, the place she finally steps into.
🔵 THE FRIEND IN BLUE The only person not on the ride is her friend, standing on the ground, dressed in the same blue. She never says "leave him". She asks one quiet question, "To where?", and the honest answer is "nowhere". Instead of answering, she tells the story from last week. The friend is love seen from outside the loop: she can see the whole circle because she is not spinning. She cannot pull anyone off. She can only stay on solid ground, so there is somewhere to land.
💛 MORE SYMBOLS • Six amber waxwork couples: the fight, the silence, the coffee, the joke, the dance, the look away. One frozen moment of every week. • The natural turn: dancing as hard as they can over the same patch of grass. Effort without distance. • The offered hand: every time they come apart he simply holds out his hand. In the last chorus she doesn't reach. • Curves, then a straight line: every camera move is an arc until she steps off. Her walk away is the first straight path in the film. • Gold ride, blue field: the safe, familiar loop versus the cold, quiet, real world. • The lanterns: when she walks away they light one by one beside her. Leaving is not a tragedy here, it is a path. • He is not the villain: "You're not pretending, not unkind. You just don't mind." The song ends with him still circling, smiling, and her watching him go by.
🎤 LYRICS [Verse 1] Sunday night we say it's over. Monday morning, you're at my shoulder with coffee, sorry, that half-smile, and I forget it for a while. We know the steps. We know the song: who storms out first, who waits how long. You know the line that brings me back. I know the joke that makes you laugh.
[Pre-Chorus] And it feels so much like flying when the music starts to swell, but the same blue tent keeps passing, and I know it far too well.
[Chorus] We go round in pretty circles, and we call it getting far. All the lights, the painted horses, and we end up where we are. It's a lovely way to travel if you never want to land. Every time we come unravelled, you just offer me your hand.
[Verse 2] A friend asks, "How are you two doing?" I say, "We're good. We just keep moving." She says, "To where?" I start to speak and tell the story from last week. And you, you're happy on this ride. You love the tune, the rise and glide. You're not pretending, not unkind. You just don't mind. You just don't mind.
[Pre-Chorus] (repeat)
[Chorus] (repeat)
[Bridge] So when the song comes round again, I let go of the painted mane. One foot down on solid ground, and nothing, nothing spins around.
[Final Chorus] You go round in pretty circles, and you wave each time you're near. All the lights, the painted horses, and I'm standing still, right here. It's a lovely way to travel. I just found I want to land. Next time round, when we unravel, I won't reach to take your hand.
[Outro] You look so happy, going by. Going by. Going by.

media:group.media:title: Make It Hard to Leave — R4agRek0il | Official Music Video
media:group.media:description:
🌙 At 2:30 in the morning, “stay” sounds a lot like a promise. By daylight, you wonder who actually made it.
🎬 *Make It Hard to Leave* | R4agRek0il | Official Animated Music Video
🎧 A R4agRek0il original. Music and vocals created with Suno.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🎵 *Lyrics* ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[Verse 1] You call me after half past two. I let it ring. I know it's you. You ask if I'm still up this late; I'm dressed before you say, "I'll wait."
I tell myself it's just a drive. Your building comes. I circle twice. You open up; I lose my place. I'd planned a speech. You touch my face.
[Pre-Chorus] You take my hand. I lose my thread. There goes the speech inside my head. One word from you could make me go. Why do I hope you tell me no?
[Chorus] Make it hard to leave. Give me more than make-believe. Don't say "stay" to pass the time, Then wake up with a change of mind. I can take a clean goodbye; It's the almosts that survive.
[Instrumental Hook]
[Verse 2] You know the songs I used to play. You skip the one that makes me stay. We laugh until the chorus ends; For half a song, we're us again.
Then "Keep it simple" cuts right through. That word means something else to you. You mean no plans, no asking why. I hear another half-goodbye.
[Pre-Chorus] You take my hand. I lose my thread. There goes the speech inside my head. One word from you could make me go. Why do I hope you tell me no?
[Chorus] Make it hard to leave. Give me more than make-believe. Don't say "stay" to pass the time, Then wake up with a change of mind. I can take a clean goodbye; It's the almosts that survive.
[Instrumental Hook]
[Bridge] You never promised me a year. You only said you liked me here. I heard a life in "Stay till dawn." You meant a song. I sang along.
[Final Chorus] I can want to stay And still choose to walk away. You can want me for tonight; I can't make your tomorrow mine. I can take a clean goodbye; It's the almosts that survive.
[Outro] Your name comes up. I watch it ring. For once, I don't do anything.
💭 * The Feeling Behind the lyrics*
The first call — He lets it ring to prove he has a choice. His clothes are already on. At the door — He’s driven around twice rehearsing what to say. Then she touches his face, and he’d give anything to stay another minute. The chorus — He asks her to make leaving hard because he wants to hear that she’ll miss him tomorrow. Their song — For half a chorus they laugh like they used to. “Keep it simple” hurts more after that. “Stay till dawn” — She meant this evening. He pictured a life. He can finally admit that both of them meant what they said. The last call — He still wants to answer. This time, he lets it ring. 📱

media:group.media:description:
6:15 AM. A familiar station. A train she's taken countless times. Everything in her life is going according to plan.
So why does she suddenly wonder whether she has to follow it? One question changes everything:
*WHAT IF I DON'T?*
An original song and animated music video by *R4agRek0il* about the freedom to question a life that looks perfectly fine from the outside.
There is no disaster. No betrayal. No one to blame.
Sometimes, the hardest decision is walking away from a perfectly good life; not because it was wrong, but because you want to discover what else is possible.
*WHAT IF I DON'T? — OFFICIAL ANIMATED MUSIC VIDEO*

*Verse 1*
Six-fifteen, the platform shakes, A paper cup against my palm. I know this journey like a prayer, Every turning, every stop.
I've got my name upon a door, A little money put aside. I used to call this everything. When did it stop feeling like mine?
*Pre-Chorus*
There's no disaster, no one to blame, No broken promise, no goodbye. But every day I hear a question I keep pretending isn't mine.
*Chorus*
What if I don't? What if I let this train go by? What if the plans I made at nineteen Aren't a promise for my life?
What if I don't? What if I change my mind? I can love the life that brought me here And still choose another one.
*Instrumental Hook*
*Verse 2*
My father calls at half past ten. He asks me how my week has been. I say, "It's good." And that's the truth. That's what makes it hard to speak.
I have no city picked out yet, No grand adventure I can name. Just a feeling I can't shake That something ought to change.
*Pre-Chorus*
How do I tell the ones I love I'm not unhappy, just not done? That I could stay and be all right, But there's a life I haven't tried.
*Chorus*
What if I don't? What if I let this train go by? What if the plans I made at nineteen Aren't a promise for my life?
What if I don't? What if I change my mind? I can love the life that brought me here And still choose another one.
*Bridge*
And if I come back in a year, To the same street, the same front door, I hope it's because I missed this place, Not because I feared much more.
Maybe I'll find that I was wrong. Maybe this is where I belong. But I'd like to know I chose to stay, Instead of letting years decide.
*Final Chorus*
What if I don't? What if I let this train go by? What if the plans I made at nineteen Were only plans, not my whole life?
What if I don't? What if I change my mind? I can love the life that brought me here And still choose another one.
*Outro*
Six-fifteen pulls out of sight. The world goes on.
And so do I.
*Instrumental Ending*

media:group.media:description:
*LOST THE COUNT — Official Animated Music Video | R4agRek0il*
What if losing your rhythm was the first step toward finding yourself?
In a world where everyone is expected to move at the same pace, one person discovers the courage to stop pretending.
"Lost the Count" is an original cinematic electro-pop song about expectations, emotional exhaustion, vulnerability, and the freedom to choose your own path.
Sometimes, losing the count is how we finally learn to live.
🎧 *Best experienced with headphones.*
🎬 *ABOUT THE STORY*
In a mechanical city, glowing regulators control every person's movements and guide their lives along predetermined paths.
Our protagonist struggles to keep pace until they make a terrifying decision: remove the regulator and experience life without guaranteed certainty.
When a stranger chooses to do the same, one small act of courage begins transforming the entire city.
A story about conformity, sacrifice, connection, and collective freedom.
